item.title: The schema and the store
item.description:
The schema

A poll and its options, in store/schema.sql. A question and an option can’t be empty, and a poll’s options are unique by position and by text:

CREATE TABLE polls (
 id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 question text NOT NULL CHECK (question <> ''),
 created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE options (
 id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
 poll_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES polls (id),
 position integer NOT NULL,
 text text NOT NULL CHECK (text <> ''),
 UNIQUE (poll_id, id),
 UNIQUE (poll_id, position),
 UNIQUE (poll_id, text)
);

A vote’s primary key is its poll and its voter, so a browser has one vote on each poll. Its foreign key names the poll as well as the option, which UNIQUE (poll_id, id) allows, so a vote is always for an option of its own poll:

item.title: Every replica
item.description:
The notification

A trigger on votes notifies the votes channel with the poll’s id, in the vote’s own transaction. PostgreSQL delivers a notification only when its transaction commits, so a vote that rolls back tells no one:

CREATE FUNCTION notify_vote() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
 PERFORM pg_notify('votes', NEW.poll_id::text);
 RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER votes_notify AFTER INSERT ON votes FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION notify_vote();

The listener

Each replica has one Listener, which every feed on the replica subscribes to:

item.title: The Site
item.description:
The paths

Every page, action and script is a typed path, and the same value routes a request and builds its links. A poll’s id must look like a UUID, so any other path is a 404:

var (
	scriptHash = hypermedia.PathParam[string]("hash")
	scriptName = hypermedia.PathParam[string]("script")
	scriptPath = hypermedia.Root().Lit("scripts").Param(scriptHash).Rest(scriptName)
	pollID = hypermedia.PathParam[string]("pollId").Pattern(regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`))
	homePath = hypermedia.Root()
	pollsPath = hypermedia.Root().Lit("polls")
	pollPath = pollsPath.Param(pollID)
	votesPath = pollPath.Lit("votes")
	feedPath = pollPath.Lit("feed")
)

The routes

One route for each method and path:

item.title: Creating a poll
item.description:
The form

The home page is the form. It posts as a plain form, and htmx posts it with hx-post and swaps the answer in its place:

{{define "main"}}<h1>Polls</h1>
{{template "form" .Form}}{{end}}{{define "form"}}<form id="new-poll" method="post" action="{{.Action}}" hx-post="{{.Action}}" hx-swap="outerHTML">
{{template "field" .Question}}
{{range .Options}}{{template "field" .}}
{{end}}<button type="submit">Create the poll</button>
</form>{{end}}{{define "field"}}<p><label>{{.Label}} <input name="{{.Name}}" value="{{.Value}}" maxlength="{{.MaxLength}}"{{if .Required}} required{{end}}></label>{{with .Problem}} <span class="problem">{{.}}</span>{{end}}</p>{{end}}{{template "layout" .}}

Its view holds each field’s value and problem, to render the form again:

type field struct {
	Name string
	Label string
	Value string
	Problem string
	MaxLength int
	Required bool
}

type pollForm struct {
	Action string
	Question field
	Options []field
}

func newPollForm() pollForm {
	f := pollForm{
		Action: pollsPath.URL().String(),
		Question: field{Name: "question", Label: "Question", MaxLength: questionMaxLength, Required: true},
	}
	for i := range optionCount {
		f.Options = append(f.Options, field{
			Name: fmt.Sprintf("option%d", i+1),
			Label: fmt.Sprintf("Option %d", i+1),
			MaxLength: optionMaxLength,
			Required: i < requiredOptions,
		})
	}
	return f
}

type homeView struct {
	Title string
	Form pollForm
}

func (ui *UI) home(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) error {
	return ui.render(w, http.StatusOK, "home.html", homeView{Title: "Polls", Form: newPollForm()})
}

The fields

The fields are declared once, with their rules: a question, and five options, the first two required. A value of only spaces breaks notBlank:

item.title: Voting
item.description:
The poll’s page

A poll’s page shows its results, and a button for each option. The results fragment is what a vote swaps:

{{define "main"}}<h1>{{.Question}}</h1>
<div hx-ext="sse" sse-connect="{{.FeedURL}}">
{{template "results" .Results}}
</div>
<p><a href="{{.HomeURL}}">Create another poll</a></p>{{end}}{{define "results"}}<div id="results">
<ul id="options" sse-swap="results">
{{template "options" .Options}}</ul>
{{with .Note}}<p class="note">{{.}}</p>
{{end}}{{with .Action}}<form method="post" action="{{.}}" hx-post="{{.}}" hx-target="#results" hx-swap="outerHTML">
{{range $.Options}}<button type="submit" name="option" value="{{.ID}}">{{.Text}}</button>
{{end}}</form>
{{end}}</div>{{end}}{{define "options"}}{{range .}}<li><span class="option">{{.Text}}</span> <span class="votes">{{.Votes}}</span></li>
{{end}}{{end}}{{template "layout" .}}

type pollView struct {
	Title string
	Question string
	Results resultsView
	FeedURL string
	HomeURL string
}

type resultsView struct {
	Options []store.Option
	Note string
	Action string
}

func votesURL(id uuid.UUID) string {
	return votesPath.URL(hypermedia.Arg(pollID, id.String())).String()
}

The handler reads the poll, and gives the browser its voter cookie before it votes:

item.title: Live results
item.description:
On the page

The poll’s page connects to its feed with htmx’s SSE extension, from the div around its results:

<div hx-ext="sse" sse-connect="{{.FeedURL}}">
{{template "results" .Results}}
</div>

Each results event replaces the options’ list with the options fragment it carries:

<ul id="options" sse-swap="results">
{{template "options" .Options}}</ul>

The feed

The feed subscribes to the poll before it reads it, so a vote between the two isn’t missed. It sends the poll’s results first, then each change:

item.title: Init
item.description:
The settings

Everything Init reads, in one struct:

type settings struct {
	HTTP httpserver.Settings
	Database *pgxpool.Config
	TrustCAs *x509.CertPool
}

type serverCertificate = func(*tls.ClientHelloInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error)

config.Struct sources and checks each one. A bad one makes Init fail, and the service exits 78, naming its variable:

func readSettings(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup, h humus.Host) (settings, error) {
	d := httpserver.DefaultSettings()
	env := func(name string) config.Value[string] { return config.Env(s.Process.Environment, name) }
	file := func(name string) config.Value[[]byte] { return env(name).Parse(readFile(h.Filesystem)) }
	timeout := func(name string, def time.Duration, check func(time.Duration) error) config.Value[time.Duration] {
		return env(name).Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(def).Validate(check)
	}

	read, err := config.Struct(func(r *config.Resolver) settings {
		server := d
		server.Addr = r.Get(env("ADDR").Validate(httpserver.CheckAddr))
		server.TLS = &tls.Config{
			GetCertificate: r.Get(env("TLS_CERT_FILE").Validate(holdsCertificate(h.Filesystem)).FlatMap(func(certFile string) config.Value[serverCertificate] {
				return env("TLS_KEY_FILE").Parse(func(keyFile string) (serverCertificate, error) {
					cfg, err := certfile.Config(h.Filesystem, certFile, keyFile)
					if err != nil {
						return nil, err
					}
					return cfg.GetCertificate, nil
				})
			})),
		}
		server.ReadHeaderTimeout = r.Get(timeout("READ_HEADER_TIMEOUT", d.ReadHeaderTimeout, httpserver.CheckReadHeaderTimeout))
		server.ReadTimeout = r.Get(timeout("READ_TIMEOUT", d.ReadTimeout, httpserver.CheckReadTimeout))
		server.WriteTimeout = r.Get(timeout("WRITE_TIMEOUT", d.WriteTimeout, httpserver.CheckWriteTimeout))
		server.IdleTimeout = r.Get(timeout("IDLE_TIMEOUT", d.IdleTimeout, httpserver.CheckIdleTimeout))
		return settings{
			HTTP: server,
			Database: r.Get(file("DATABASE_URL_FILE").Parse(databaseURL)),
			TrustCAs: r.Get(env("FAULT_TRUST_CA_FILE").Parse(trustCAs(h.Filesystem)).Default(nil)),
		}
	}).Read(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return settings{}, err
	}
	if read.TrustCAs != nil {
		read.HTTP.TLS.ClientAuth = tls.VerifyClientCertIfGiven
		read.HTTP.TLS.ClientCAs = read.TrustCAs
		read.HTTP.TrustScenario = issuedByATrustedCA
	}
	return read, nil
}

The certificate’s file is checked on its own before the pair is read, so a file that holds no certificate is an error that names TLS_CERT_FILE, not TLS_KEY_FILE.

item.title: Testing
item.description:
The Site’s unit tests

The Site’s tests serve it on the humustest Host, with a Store of their own:

	p, status := httpservertest.Start(t, h.Host(), func(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup, h humus.Host) ([]humus.Service, error) {
		settings := httpserver.DefaultSettings()
		settings.Addr = "polls.internal:8443"
		settings.TLS = &tls.Config{Certificates: []tls.Certificate{cert.TLS()}}
		u, err := ui.New(polls, polls, settings.WriteTimeout)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		site, err := u.Site(s)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		svc, err := httpserver.NewService(ctx, s, h, settings, site)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return []humus.Service{svc}, nil
	}, humustest.WithApp(append([]humus.Option{}, opts...)...))

Each test runs inside synctest, and checks the HTML a request gets:

item.title: Deploying
item.description:
The image

A Go stage builds the service static:

RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go -C example/http/polls build -trimpath -ldflags=-s -o /out/polls .

The image copies it to /polls on a distroless base, to run as the non-root user 65532:

COPY --from=build /out/polls /polls
USER 65532:65532

example/http/polls/Dockerfile names the exact images and their versions.

Build it from the repository’s root, since the module replaces humus with its directory:

docker build --file example/http/polls/Dockerfile --tag polls .

The kustomization

deploy/base holds a ServiceAccount, the Deployment, its Service and its disruption budget, and the service’s settings:

item.title: Observing
item.description:
Opening Grafana

up.sh generates Grafana’s admin password into the grafana-admin Secret. Read it, then forward Grafana’s port:

kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace polls get secret grafana-admin \
 --output jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode
kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace polls port-forward service/grafana 3000:3000

Sign in at http://localhost:3000 as admin.

A vote’s trace

Vote on a poll, as Trying it in a browser shows. Each server span is named after its method and its route, so in Explore, with Tempo, find the votes by their name:

item.title: Production-ready
item.description:
The polls service meets each item. Check your own hypermedia UI against it:

Item How Where
Every setting sourced and checked; a bad one exits 78, naming its variable config.Struct and the packages’ checks, in readSettings The settings, Every variable it reads
No secret in the environment, the logs or the spans the database URL and the certificate’s key are files, read through s.Host.Filesystem. No voter cookie or database password is recorded, which a test of the App checks The secrets and certificates, as files, Its log records
Certificates renewed without a restart internal/certfile, which reads the files again when they change, so a renewed Secret needs no restart. A test of the App renews the certificate under a running server The certificate, read again when renewed
Two replicas a PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable: 1, and a rolling update of maxUnavailable: 0 The Deployment, The disruption budget
Ready only once it has reached PostgreSQL and its listener has listened, and still ready through an outage the latching monitors, on the probes beside the Site Readiness, The probes
A rollout loses no request httpserver.Main’s 5s drain, and a terminationGracePeriodSeconds above the drain, the grace period and the telemetry’s shutdown The drain
Least privilege the service’s role only reads and inserts, so it changes no schema and no vote. A non-root, read-only container. No service account token mounted The roles, The kustomization, The Deployment
Observable traces, logs and metrics over OTLP, the alerts in deploy/alerts.yaml, deploy/dashboard.json, and alerts on the Deployment from the Collector’s Kubernetes cluster receiver A vote’s trace, Its log records, The metrics, The alerts, The dashboard
Failures say why an error page for each status: a 503 for a database that is down, a 404, a 409 for a second vote, and a 422 that shows each problem in place The error page, The 422, One vote per browser
Failures are rehearsed the failure injection cases on postgresql:polls, in CI, and against an end user’s staging through its own Target The injection point, The failure injection cases
Safe by default FAULT_TRUST_CA_FILE empty, so no scenario is trusted TrustScenario
One vote per browser, kept by the database a __Host- voter cookie, and a vote’s primary key of its poll and its voter, so two votes sent at once count once The schema, Voting, The voter cookie
Cross-site votes refused http.CrossOriginProtection around the Site, answered by the 403 page, and every vote a POST Cross-origin requests
Scripts from the service’s own origin only, under the CSP htmx and its SSE extension vendored, at content-hashed URLs, and script-src 'self' with nothing inline. The browser cases check that no page reports a CSP violation The scripts, The Site and its CSP, The browser cases, on kind
Results on every replica a trigger that notifies on the vote’s commit, and a listener on each replica that hands the results to its feeds The notification, The listener, The shared cases
An open page that keeps updating through a rollout, which exits 0 each open feed ends cleanly as Shutdown begins, and htmx connects it again to a replica that is still serving. Each replica exits 0 on SIGTERM At Shutdown, Init’s unit tests, The browser cases, on kind
